subject: B
topic: Sectional revision — GK & Current Affairs India

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Regulating Act of 1773 is significant because it:
options: Established the post of Governor-General of Bengal and a Supreme Court at Calcutta
Introduced the system of Dyarchy in provinces
Abolished the East India Company's trade monopoly
Granted Indians the right to vote for the first time
questions.correctAnswer: Established the post of Governor-General of Bengal and a Supreme Court at Calcutta
questions.explanation: 'Established the post of Governor-General of Bengal and a Supreme Court at Calcutta' is correct — the Regulating Act (1773) created the office of Governor-General (Warren Hastings was first) and a Supreme Court at Calcutta. 'Dyarchy' is wrong — that was introduced by the Government of India Act 1919. 'Abolished trade monopoly' is wrong — that was the Charter Act of 1813. 'Right to vote' is wrong — limited franchise came much later.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Monsoon:

(i) The South-West monsoon accounts for about 75% of India's annual rainfall.
(ii) The monsoon enters India through the coast of Kerala around June 1.
(iii) The retreating monsoon brings rainfall mainly to Tamil Nadu's Coromandel coast.
(iv) The monsoon is entirely predictable and arrives on the exact same date every year.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the SW monsoon (June–September) contributes ~75% of total annual rainfall. (ii) is correct — the monsoon typically arrives in Kerala by June 1 (±7 days). (iii) is correct — the retreating monsoon (NE monsoon, Oct–Dec) brings rain to Tamil Nadu. (iv) is wrong — monsoon arrival dates vary; the IMD provides forecasts, but exact dates fluctuate due to climatic variables.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Right to Information Act' came into force on:
questions.explanation: '12 October 2005' is correct — the RTI Act received Presidential assent on 15 June 2005 and came fully into force on 12 October 2005. '26 January 2006' is wrong — the Act was operational before this date. '15 August 2005' is wrong — while the Act was passed earlier in 2005, it came into force in October. '2 October 2005' is wrong — this date is not associated with the RTI's implementation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Deccan Plateau is rich in black soil (Regur soil).
Reason (R): Black soil is formed from the weathering of volcanic basalt rocks (Deccan Trap) and is highly suitable for cotton cultivation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, MP) has extensive black/regur soil. (R) is correct — black soil forms from basaltic lava (Deccan Trap) weathering and is excellent for cotton (hence 'black cotton soil'). (R) explains (A) because the Deccan Trap volcanic origin is the geological reason for black soil presence. Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following important days with their dates:

Column I:
(a) Republic Day
(b) Independence Day
(c) Gandhi Jayanti
(d) Constitution Day

Column II:
(i) 15 August
(ii) 26 November
(iii) 2 October
(iv) 26 January

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(iv): Republic Day is on 26 January. (b)-(i): Independence Day is on 15 August. (c)-(iii): Gandhi Jayanti is on 2 October. (d)-(ii): Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is on 26 November (the day the Constitution was adopted in 1949). The other options incorrectly pair days with dates.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The largest freshwater lake in India is:
questions.explanation: 'Wular Lake (J&K)' is correct — Wular Lake in Bandipora district is India's largest freshwater lake. 'Chilika Lake' is wrong — it is a brackish water lake (India's largest lagoon), not freshwater. 'Dal Lake' is wrong — while in J&K, it is much smaller than Wular Lake. 'Vembanad Lake' is wrong — it is a brackish water lake in Kerala, the longest lake in India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched (Crop — Major Producing State)?

(i) Tea — Assam
(ii) Coffee — Karnataka
(iii) Rubber — Tamil Nadu
(iv) Jute — West Bengal

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Assam is India's largest tea-producing state. (ii) is correct — Karnataka (Coorg, Chikmagalur) is India's largest coffee producer. (iv) is correct — West Bengal is the leading jute-producing state. (iii) is wrong — Kerala (not Tamil Nadu) is India's largest rubber-producing state.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Panchayati Raj System:

(i) It has a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zila Parishad.
(ii) The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave it constitutional status.
(iii) Elections are conducted every 7 years.
(iv) One-third of seats are reserved for women.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the three-tier structure operates at village, block, and district levels. (ii) is correct — the 73rd Amendment constitutionalized Panchayati Raj. (iv) is correct — not less than 1/3 seats are reserved for women (Article 243D). (iii) is wrong — elections are held every 5 years, not 7 (Article 243E).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is called a 'subcontinent'.
Reason (R): India has distinct geographical features — lofty mountains, vast plains, plateaus, deserts, and coastlines — giving it a continental character despite being part of Asia.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — India is referred to as a subcontinent due to its size and geographical diversity. (R) is correct — its varied terrain (Himalayas, Indo-Gangetic plains, Deccan Plateau, Thar Desert, extensive coastline) gives it a self-contained continental character. (R) explains (A) because this geographical diversity is what qualifies it as a 'subcontinent'. Option 2 is wrong because R explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Fundamental Rights' in the Indian Constitution was inspired by the constitution of:
questions.explanation: 'USA' is correct — the concept of justiciable Fundamental Rights was borrowed from the US Bill of Rights. 'UK' is wrong — the UK has no codified Bill of Rights in its unwritten constitution; India borrowed parliamentary government from UK. 'Ireland' is wrong — DPSP (non-justiciable guidelines) were borrowed from Ireland. 'France' is wrong — ideals of Liberty, Equality, Fraternity in the Preamble came from France.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The longest river in peninsular India is the __________.
questions.explanation: 'Godavari' is correct — at approximately 1,465 km, the Godavari is the longest river in peninsular India (and second longest in India after the Ganga). 'Krishna' is wrong — it is about 1,400 km, slightly shorter than the Godavari. 'Narmada' is wrong — it is about 1,312 km. 'Kaveri' is wrong — it is about 800 km, much shorter.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Constitutional Amendments with their significance:

Column I:
(a) 42nd Amendment (1976)
(b) 44th Amendment (1978)
(c) 61st Amendment (1988)
(d) 86th Amendment (2002)

Column II:
(i) Reduced voting age from 21 to 18
(ii) Added 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' to the Preamble
(iii) Right to Education as a Fundamental Right
(iv) Right to Property made a legal right (not fundamental)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(ii): The 42nd Amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' to the Preamble. (b)-(iv): The 44th Amendment removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights. (c)-(i): The 61st Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18. (d)-(iii): The 86th Amendment made free education for 6–14 year-olds a Fundamental Right. The other options misassign amendments.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Sarvodaya' movement was associated with:
questions.explanation: 'Vinoba Bhave' is correct — Vinoba Bhave led the Sarvodaya (welfare of all) and Bhoodan (land gift) movements inspired by Gandhian principles. 'Jawaharlal Nehru' is wrong — he focused on nation-building through planning and industrialization. 'Subhas Chandra Bose' is wrong — he led the INA and militant nationalism. 'B.R. Ambedkar' is wrong — he championed Dalit rights and constitutional reforms.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched (Dance Form — State)?

(i) Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh
(ii) Kathakali — Kerala
(iii) Sattriya — Assam
(iv) Mohiniyattam — Tamil Nadu

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Kuchipudi originated in Andhra Pradesh (Kuchipudi village, Krishna district). (ii) is correct — Kathakali is a classical dance-drama from Kerala. (iii) is correct — Sattriya is a classical dance from Assam, originating in Vaishnavite monasteries. (iv) is wrong — Mohiniyattam is from Kerala, not Tamil Nadu (Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world.
Reason (R): It incorporates provisions from numerous foreign constitutions and addresses the diverse needs of a large, heterogeneous population.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — with 395+ articles and 12 schedules (originally), it is the world's longest written constitution. (R) is correct — borrowing from multiple sources and addressing India's diversity (castes, religions, languages, federal/unitary balance) contributed to its length. (R) explains (A) because these factors directly explain why the Constitution needed to be so detailed. Option 2 is wrong because R explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Project Tiger' was launched in India in which year?
questions.explanation: '1973' is correct — Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 under PM Indira Gandhi to protect the Royal Bengal Tiger from extinction. '1980' is wrong — by then the project had been running for 7 years. '1972' is wrong — the Wildlife Protection Act was passed in 1972, but Project Tiger started in 1973. '1985' is wrong — well after the project's launch.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List:

(i) Defence, Foreign Affairs, and Banking are in the Union List.
(ii) Police and Public Health are in the State List.
(iii) Education and Forests are in the Concurrent List.
(iv) Agriculture is exclusively in the Union List.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Defence (Entry 1), Foreign Affairs (Entry 10), Banking (Entry 45) are all in the Union List. (ii) is correct — Police (Entry 2) and Public Health (Entry 6) are in the State List. (iii) is correct — Education (Entry 25) and Forests (Entry 17A) were moved to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment. (iv) is wrong — Agriculture is in the State List (Entry 14), not the Union List.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Simon Commission visited India in which year?
questions.explanation: '1928' is correct — the Simon Commission arrived in India in February 1928 to review the working of the Government of India Act 1919. '1919' is wrong — this is when the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were implemented. '1935' is wrong — the Government of India Act was passed in 1935 based partly on Simon Commission recommendations. '1930' is wrong — the First Round Table Conference was in 1930.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Inter-State Council was established under Article __________ of the Indian Constitution.
questions.explanation: '263' is correct — Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council for coordination between states and Centre. '256' is wrong — it deals with obligation of States to comply with Union laws. '280' is wrong — it deals with the Finance Commission. '312' is wrong — it deals with All India Services.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Mughal Emperors with their achievements:

Column I:
(a) Akbar
(b) Shah Jahan
(c) Jahangir
(d) Aurangzeb

Column II:
(i) Built the Taj Mahal
(ii) Extended the Mughal Empire to its greatest territorial extent
(iii) Founded Din-i-Ilahi and abolished Jaziya
(iv) Known as patron of painting and justice (Chain of Justice)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(iii): Akbar founded Din-i-Ilahi and abolished Jaziya (tax on non-Muslims). (b)-(i): Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal. (c)-(iv): Jahangir was a patron of painting and installed the 'Chain of Justice' (Zanjir-i-Adl). (d)-(ii): Aurangzeb expanded the Mughal Empire to its greatest extent (including the Deccan). The other options misassign achievements.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Pokhran-II' nuclear tests (1998) were conducted under the code name:
questions.explanation: 'Operation Shakti' is correct — the Pokhran-II nuclear tests (May 1998) conducted under PM Vajpayee were codenamed Operation Shakti. 'Operation Vijay' is wrong — it was the code name for the Kargil War (1999). 'Operation Meghdoot' is wrong — it was the 1984 operation to capture the Siachen Glacier. 'Operation Parakram' is wrong — it was the 2001–02 military mobilization after the Parliament attack.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha does not vote in normal circumstances.
Reason (R): The Speaker has a casting vote which can be exercised only in the case of a tie to maintain impartiality in presiding over the House.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Speaker abstains from voting ordinarily to maintain neutrality. (R) is correct — Article 100 gives the Speaker a casting vote only when there is an equality of votes (tie). (R) explains (A) because having only a casting vote (in ties) is the constitutional provision that keeps the Speaker impartial. Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Scheduled Languages under the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?

(i) Hindi
(ii) English
(iii) Dogri
(iv) Kashmiri

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Hindi is a Scheduled Language. (iii) is correct — Dogri was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003). (iv) is correct — Kashmiri is a Scheduled Language. (ii) is wrong — English is NOT a Scheduled Language under the Eighth Schedule; it is used as an associate official language but not listed in the schedule.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The famous 'Dandi March' covered a distance of approximately:
questions.explanation: '385 km from Sabarmati to Dandi' is correct — Gandhi marched 385 km (240 miles) from Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad to Dandi, Gujarat in 24 days (12 March – 6 April 1930). 'Delhi to Agra' is wrong — the Dandi March was entirely in Gujarat. 'Calcutta to Dhaka' is wrong — unrelated route. 'Pune to Mumbai' is wrong — the march was not in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following institutions with their locations:

Column I:
(a) Indian Military Academy (IMA)
(b) National Defence Academy (NDA)
(c) Indian Naval Academy
(d) Air Force Academy

Column II:
(i) Khadakwasla (Pune)
(ii) Dehradun
(iii) Ezhimala (Kerala)
(iv) Dundigal (Hyderabad)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(ii): IMA is in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. (b)-(i): NDA is at Khadakwasla, near Pune. (c)-(iii): Indian Naval Academy is at Ezhimala, Kerala. (d)-(iv): Air Force Academy is at Dundigal, Hyderabad. The other options incorrectly pair institutions with locations.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The National Anthem of India 'Jana Gana Mana' was first sung on:
questions.explanation: '27 December 1911' is correct — 'Jana Gana Mana' by Rabindranath Tagore was first sung at the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress on 27 December 1911. '26 January 1950' is wrong — it was adopted as the National Anthem on 24 January 1950, not first sung then. '15 August 1947' is wrong — Independence Day, but the song was first performed decades earlier. '24 January 1950' is wrong — this is the date of adoption, not first performance.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:

(i) It is constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution.
(ii) It recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and States.
(iii) It is a permanent body that functions continuously.
(iv) The 15th Finance Commission submitted its report for the period 2021–26.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission. (ii) is correct — the FC recommends the vertical (Centre-States) and horizontal (among States) distribution of tax revenues. (iv) is correct — the 15th FC (chaired by N.K. Singh) covers 2021–2026. (iii) is wrong — the Finance Commission is constituted every five years; it is not a permanent body.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Swadeshi Movement' was launched as a response to:
questions.explanation: 'The Partition of Bengal (1905)' is correct — Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal triggered the Swadeshi Movement, promoting Indian-made goods and boycotting British products. 'Jallianwala Bagh Massacre' is wrong — it led to the Non-Cooperation Movement. 'Rowlatt Act' is wrong — opposition to it led to protests including Jallianwala Bagh. 'Salt Tax' is wrong — Gandhi's Salt March (1930) addressed this.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Fundamental Rights can be suspended during a National Emergency.
Reason (R): Article 358 and 359 provide for automatic suspension of Articles 19 and Presidential orders suspending other rights during emergency.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — during a National Emergency, Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21, post-44th Amendment) can be suspended. (R) is correct — Article 358 automatically suspends Article 19 during external emergency; Article 359 allows the President to suspend enforcement of other rights. (R) explains (A) by citing the specific constitutional provisions that enable suspension. Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) launched the Chandrayaan-3 mission, which landed on the Moon's south pole region on:
questions.explanation: '23 August 2023' is correct — the Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-3 soft-landed near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to achieve this. '14 July 2023' is wrong — that was the launch date from Sriharikota. '5 September 2023' is wrong — by then the Pragyan rover had already completed its mission. '23 August 2022' is wrong — wrong year; the mission was in 2023.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements about the Indian judiciary are correct?

(i) The Supreme Court is the guardian of the Constitution.
(ii) India has an integrated judicial system.
(iii) High Court judges are appointed by the State Governors.
(iv) The Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Supreme Court is the guardian and final interpreter of the Constitution. (ii) is correct — India has a single integrated judiciary (Supreme Court → High Courts → District Courts). (iv) is correct — the SC has original jurisdiction (disputes between Centre/States), appellate (appeals from HCs), and advisory (Art. 143). (iii) is wrong — High Court judges are appointed by the President (after consultation with the CJI and Governor), not by State Governors alone.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Permanent Settlement' of 1793 was introduced by:
questions.explanation: 'Lord Cornwallis' is correct — Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha, fixing the land revenue in perpetuity. 'Lord Wellesley' is wrong — he introduced the Subsidiary Alliance System. 'Lord Dalhousie' is wrong — he introduced the Doctrine of Lapse. 'Warren Hastings' is wrong — he preceded Cornwallis and had different revenue policies.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The data below shows India's GDP growth rate (%) over four years:

2019–20 → 4.0
2020–21 → –7.3
2021–22 → 8.7
2022–23 → 7.2

Which year showed the maximum positive change compared to the previous year?
questions.explanation: Changes from previous year: 2020–21: –7.3 – 4.0 = –11.3 (decrease). 2021–22: 8.7 – (–7.3) = +16.0 (increase). 2022–23: 7.2 – 8.7 = –1.5 (decrease). The maximum positive change is in 2021–22 (+16 percentage points swing). '2022–23' is wrong — the rate actually decreased. '2019–20' is wrong — we can't calculate change without 2018–19 data. '2020–21' is wrong — it showed a massive negative change.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following soils with the regions where they are predominantly found:

Column I:
(a) Alluvial soil
(b) Black (Regur) soil
(c) Laterite soil
(d) Red soil

Column II:
(i) Deccan Trap region (Maharashtra, Gujarat)
(ii) Indo-Gangetic Plains
(iii) Eastern Deccan Plateau (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka)
(iv) Western Ghats, Meghalaya Plateau

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(ii): Alluvial soil is found in the Indo-Gangetic Plains (deposited by rivers). (b)-(i): Black/Regur soil covers the Deccan Trap region (Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP). (c)-(iv): Laterite soil is found in heavy rainfall areas (Western Ghats, Meghalaya). (d)-(iii): Red soil is found in the eastern Deccan Plateau regions (parts of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Odisha). The other options misassign soils.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Emergency Provisions' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
options: The Government of India Act, 1935 (and German Weimar Constitution)
questions.correctAnswer: The Government of India Act, 1935 (and German Weimar Constitution)
questions.explanation: 'The Government of India Act, 1935 (and German Weimar Constitution)' is correct — emergency provisions were largely inspired by the GoI Act 1935 and the Weimar Republic's emergency clauses. 'US Constitution' is wrong — the US doesn't have elaborate emergency provisions like India. 'French Constitution' is wrong — France's emergency powers differ significantly. 'Canadian Constitution' is wrong — India borrowed federation with strong centre from Canada, not emergency provisions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Chipko Movement' and 'Appiko Movement' are associated with:
questions.explanation: 'Forest conservation' is correct — Chipko (Uttarakhand, 1973) and Appiko (Karnataka, 1983) were grassroots movements against deforestation where people embraced trees. 'Water conservation' is wrong — that's associated with movements like Narmada Bachao. 'Anti-nuclear protests' is wrong — Kudankulam protests were anti-nuclear. 'Labour rights' is wrong — these movements were environmental, not labour-related.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's foreign trade:

(i) India's largest trading partner (by total trade volume) is the USA or China (varies by year).
(ii) India's major exports include petroleum products, gems/jewellery, and IT services.
(iii) India has always had a trade surplus (exports exceed imports).
(iv) The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act was enacted in 2005.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — China and USA alternate as India's largest trading partners depending on the year. (ii) is correct — petroleum products, gems/jewellery, and IT services are among India's top exports. (iv) is correct — the SEZ Act was enacted in 2005 to promote exports. (iii) is wrong — India typically has a trade DEFICIT (imports exceed exports), especially due to oil imports.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows literacy rates of Indian states:

Kerala → 96.2%
Delhi → 88.7%
Bihar → 63.8%
Rajasthan → 67.1%

What is the approximate difference between the highest and lowest literacy rates shown?
questions.explanation: Highest = Kerala (96.2%), Lowest = Bihar (63.8%). Difference = 96.2 – 63.8 = 32.4%. '28.9%' is wrong — this would require lowest to be about 67.3%. '25.1%' is wrong — this understates the gap. '35.5%' is wrong — this overstates the difference.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.
Reason (R): In a parliamentary democracy, the civilian head of state holds nominal supreme command to ensure civilian control over the military.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Article 53(2) vests supreme command of the Armed Forces in the President. (R) is correct — in parliamentary democracies, the civilian head ensures the military remains subordinate to elected government. (R) explains (A) because the principle of civilian control is the reason this power is constitutionally vested in the President. Option 2 is wrong because R explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct order of planets from the Sun (nearest to farthest)?
questions.explanation: 'Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars' is correct — this is the correct sequence of the four inner (terrestrial) planets from nearest to farthest from the Sun. 'Venus, Mercury' is wrong — Mercury is closest to the Sun, not Venus. 'Mercury, Earth, Venus' is wrong — Venus is between Mercury and Earth. 'Earth, Venus, Mercury' is wrong — this reverses the correct order.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Judicial Activism' in India refers to:
options: The proactive role of the judiciary in protecting rights and directing governance through PILs and directives
questions.correctAnswer: The proactive role of the judiciary in protecting rights and directing governance through PILs and directives
questions.explanation: 'The proactive role of the judiciary' is correct — judicial activism involves courts going beyond their traditional role by issuing directions, entertaining PILs, and monitoring government actions. 'Judges in political campaigns' is wrong — judges are prohibited from political activity. 'Courts refusing cases' is wrong — that would be the opposite of activism. 'Lawyers striking' is wrong — that is a labour action, not judicial activism.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with the seas/oceans they drain into:

Column I:
(a) Ganga
(b) Narmada
(c) Indus
(d) Brahmaputra

Column II:
(i) Bay of Bengal
(ii) Arabian Sea
(iii) Bay of Bengal (via Bangladesh)
(iv) Arabian Sea (via Pakistan)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a)-(i): Ganga drains into the Bay of Bengal (through the Sunderbans delta). (b)-(ii): Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea. (c)-(iv): Indus flows through Pakistan into the Arabian Sea. (d)-(iii): Brahmaputra flows through Bangladesh (as Jamuna/Padma) into the Bay of Bengal. The other options incorrectly pair rivers with water bodies.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi' (PM-KISAN) scheme provides:
options: ₹6,000 per year to eligible farmer families in three instalments
Free seeds and fertilizers to all farmers
questions.correctAnswer: ₹6,000 per year to eligible farmer families in three instalments
questions.explanation: '₹6,000 per year in three instalments' is correct — PM-KISAN (launched February 2019) provides ₹6,000/year (₹2,000 every 4 months) directly to farmer families. 'Free seeds and fertilizers' is wrong — these are under different subsidy schemes. '₹10,000 for crop insurance' is wrong — crop insurance is under PM Fasal Bima Yojana, a different scheme. 'Free electricity' is wrong — some states provide this independently, but it's not PM-KISAN.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:

(i) It is an independent constitutional body under Article 324.
(ii) The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed like a Supreme Court judge.
(iii) It conducts elections for President, Vice President, and Parliament.
(iv) Election Commissioners have the same removal protections as the CEC.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 324 establishes the ECI as an independent constitutional body. (ii) is correct — the CEC can only be removed through impeachment (same procedure as a SC judge). (iii) is correct — ECI conducts elections for President, VP, Parliament, and State Legislatures. (iv) is wrong — Election Commissioners do NOT have the same removal protection as the CEC; they can be removed on the CEC's recommendation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was founded in the year __________.
questions.explanation: '1969' is correct — ISRO was established on 15 August 1969, superseding the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR). '1962' is wrong — INCOSPAR was set up in 1962, but ISRO came later. '1975' is wrong — Aryabhata satellite was launched in 1975; ISRO existed earlier. '1972' is wrong — the Space Commission and Department of Space were set up in 1972, but ISRO was already established.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched (Award — Field)?

(i) Arjuna Award — Outstanding sportspersons
(ii) Padma Shri — Fourth highest civilian honour
(iii) Sahitya Akademi Award — Literature
(iv) Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize — Cinema

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Arjuna Award recognizes outstanding sportspersons. (ii) is correct — Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian honour (after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan). (iii) is correct — Sahitya Akademi Award is for literary excellence. (iv) is wrong — Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize is for Science and Technology, not Cinema (Dadasaheb Phalke Award is for cinema).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Quit India Resolution' was passed at which session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: 'Bombay Session (1942)' is correct — the Quit India Resolution was passed at the All India Congress Committee session in Bombay on 8 August 1942. 'Lahore Session (1929)' is wrong — it passed the Purna Swaraj resolution. 'Karachi Session (1931)' is wrong — it adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights. 'Tripuri Session (1939)' is wrong — it saw the contest between Bose and Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has a 'federal system with a unitary character'.
Reason (R): During emergencies, the Centre can exercise overriding authority over states, and residuary powers lie with the Union.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — India's system is federal in structure but tilts toward unitarism. (R) is correct — emergency powers converting federal to unitary, and residuary powers with the Centre (unlike the US), demonstrate unitary character. (R) explains (A) because these specific provisions create the 'unitary character' mentioned in A. Option 2 is wrong because R explains A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Balance of Trade' refers to:
options: The difference between the value of a country's exports and imports of goods
The total amount of gold reserves held by a country
The exchange rate between two currencies
The total national income of a country
questions.correctAnswer: The difference between the value of a country's exports and imports of goods
questions.explanation: 'The difference between exports and imports of goods' is correct — Balance of Trade = Export value – Import value of visible goods. A negative balance means trade deficit. 'Gold reserves' is wrong — that is part of foreign exchange reserves. 'Exchange rate' is wrong — that is the price of one currency in terms of another. 'National income' is wrong — that is GDP/GNP, a much broader concept.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of Governor-Generals of India?
questions.explanation: 'Warren Hastings → Cornwallis → Wellesley → Dalhousie' is correct — Hastings (1773–85), Cornwallis (1786–93), Wellesley (1798–1805), Dalhousie (1848–56). The other options have incorrect sequences. Note: other GGs served between these, but among these four, this is the correct order.
